question: Electronic animal health certification via TRACES is needed to transport bee colonies within the EU and to import them from third countries. This is granted on the basis of, among other things, tests for American foulbrood, Tropilaelaps mites and the small hive beetle, and is currently only valid for 10 days. In practice, the short validity period causes considerable problems.

Queen bees remain at mating stations for around two weeks to ensure successful mating. After the 10 days have expired a new certificate is required, but this can prove difficult to obtain since no sealed brood is often available for the necessary sampling.

Even for migratory beekeeping, where colonies remain in certain regions for several weeks, a new TRACES certificate is required for the return journey, even though the state of the colonies’ heath usually remains unchanged during this period. This causes avoidable red tape for beekeepers and authorities. 1.
Does the Commission plan to extend the validity of TRACES certificates for bees to up to 28 days, for transport to mating stations or migratory beekeeping for instance?
Would the Commission be prepared to certify both outward and return transport if the state of the bees’ health was evidently sound?
What conditions would be necessary for such an adjustment within the framework of EU animal health law?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2025) The EU specific animal health requirements for the movements of honeybees are laid down in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/6881 (Article 48 thereof). Among those there are no requirements related to sampling and testing of brood.

Those requirements are related to the animal health situation in the apiaries of dispatch and to the situation in the surroundings. It is appropriate that those requirements are certified within a defined time frame before each movement between Member States.

Validity of the animal health certificates is also laid down in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/688 (Article 91(3) thereof) and applies to all certificates for every species. That validity period is to cater for one movement of consignments with one certificate but not for several.

Derogations from the standard validity period and from the one movement rules are currently limited to very specific cases where those derogations are necessary and possible (e.g., for certain individual equine animals participating in races, etc.) This Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/688 which includes the above requirements for honeybees, was laid down after due discussions with experts from the Member States.
These are based on scientific risks assessments by the European Food Safety Authority and they also confirm to international standards of the World Organisation for Animal Health.

The Commission considers that the current requirements ensure safe movements of honeybees between Member States and does not plan any amendment for migratory beekeeping movements between Member States or to regulate a movement from an establishment together with a return movement to the same establishment.
